question: Loudness of sound is proportional to the ______ of the amplitude of the vibration producing the sound.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Square**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sound is produced by any kind of vibrations. 
 
• As sound waves are longitudinal waves, the air particles vibrate to and fro in the direction of the propagation of sound.
 
• It is a wave of compression and rarefaction.
 
• The amplitude of wavelength is the maximum distance the particle oscillating moves from the mean position.
 
• The frequency of the wave is the number of times one complete cycle of compressions 
 
• 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7bc73a3078186f11a5b5eb735863b0975e3720858151c33bebbb537f8c916141.png] 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The loudness of sound is related to the intensity of sound. 
 
• The loudness is directly proportional to the square of the amplitude. 

L ∝ A2

 
• It has nothing to do with the wavelength and frequency of sound. 
 
• The Pitch of the sound is determined by the frequency.
